_comment: Test files excluded from collection, with the measured reason for each. This list may only SHRINK. scripts/check_test_quarantine.py fails when a NEW file is quarantined, and ALSO fails when a listed file starts passing -- so a fixed file must be deleted from here rather than lingering as permanent amnesty. Same shape as scripts/schema_contract_baseline.json.
_origin: All 16 files were quarantined in one commit on 2026-05-23 (#362, 'working test infrastructure + pre-push hook + CI') -- the same commit that turned the gates ON. Getting a green baseline meant exempting everything that failed, and nothing ever forced a re-check. Re-measured 2026-08-09 against the live database: 5 files passed with no changes at all (35 tests) and were released. Two more were broken BY the quarantining itself; fixing the import order released a SIXTH file (test_conveyancing_integration.py, 8 passed) -- found by the ratchet on its very first run, which is the behaviour this file exists for.
_how_to_clear_an_entry: Fix the test, run scripts/check_test_quarantine.py, and it will tell you the entry is now passing and must be deleted from this file.
_deleted_2026_08_09: Five files deleted rather than repaired: test_ashfield_query, test_marrickville_query, test_ashfield_marrickville_fix, test_prp_8b_verification, test_end_to_end_user_flow. Together 1,090 lines with ZERO test functions and ZERO assert statements -- print-based one-off scripts that happened to be named test_*. They could never pass or fail, so they were not debt to repay, they were noise inflating the count. Recoverable from git history if ever wanted.
_released_as_integration_2026_08_09: test_address_validation.py and test_real_user_flow_with_pp.py are no longer quarantined. They drive a local HTTP server, so they now carry pytest.mark.integration plus a skipif that probes the server, and report as a visible SKIP with an actionable reason instead of being silently uncollected. test_address_validation additionally needed conftest._load_test_addresses to stop raising during pytest_generate_tests -- a collection-time raise cannot be reached by any skipif -- and a .gitignore escape, because the broad test_*.json rule had made its fixture impossible to commit.
_released_2026_08_09_lga_coverage: test_lga_coverage.py released. Import order repaired, and tests/conftest_mocks.py gained an opt-in (PYTEST_REAL_DB=1) so a database test can finally obtain a real connection. Without DATABASE_URL it skips cleanly, so CI stays green; with one it RUNS and immediately found a real defect: Marrickville has 14.8% NULL v2_topic (583 of 3,934) against a 10% threshold. Run it with: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... pytest tests/test_lga_coverage.py -o addopts=
_open_design_question: The gate checks only 4 hardcoded councils, in a slug format ('inner-west/marrickville') that does not even match production ('marrickville'). It does NOT read the enabled-councils list, so it cannot notice a council being switched on. Rewriting it to derive that list was attempted and STOPPED, because the check it would need to make is tier-dependent and no machine-readable tier map exists: Tier 1 councils (Inner West) promise full provision text; Tier 2 councils promise numeric controls ONLY, and having no provisions is their DESIGNED state, not a defect. Until someone records which council is on which tier, a derived gate would either pass vacuously or fail 13 councils that are working as intended. That is a product decision, not a test fix.
